structure.parsing_note: add_timing_probe_identity() attaches the sealed identity block to every recorded row while the probe is active, so a plain grep for 'rate_timing_probe' counts 82307 lines while only 27435 rows have kind='rate_timing_probe'. Analyzers filter on kind and are unaffected.

latch_reconciliation.reading: the guard crossed in the next group's release wait; the last recorded group start is still below 100 ms (99880816) and its end is below too (96205477), so no single group's start lateness explains the latch

probe_phases.reading: phase shares are shares of the entire wait, not of the excess; the decisive split is entry_lateness (before the probe entered begin_group, max 20.75 ms) versus post-entry excess (inside the measured wait, max only 0.323 ms)

dominant_events.note: entry lateness of a group equals the previous group's work overrun when the wait itself is short; the three rows below carry essentially the whole pre-entry total (20749745 + 3057160 + 2634691 = 26441596 ns vs entry_lateness_total 26515920 ns)

cpu_sections.retention_rule: slow(>2 ms) or periodic(tick%250) samples only, so these are not a full census; each wait brackets only wait_ap/wait_px4

stall_chain_tick_107572.relation: the gen-2 GC interval (333123296937..333147623903) is nested inside the px4 wait interval (333123246422..333148032847), which is inside the native_inputs stage; the px4 wait thread CPU equals its wall (24787151 vs 24786425), i.e. the supervisor was running on-CPU rather than blocked off-CPU
stall_chain_tick_107572.consequence: the group spanning tick 107572 overran by about 20.75 ms, and the next group's begin_group was entered 20749745 ns after its earliest boundary (20785815 ns post-entry excess) - 20.8 percent of the 100.050657 ms latch in one event

tail_bucket_100_500us.reading: in the creep-bearing bucket the loop_health total (56.4 ms) is at least as large as the bucket's total release excess (52.1 ms); this is a correlation inside the same wait, not a causal split (the tool states correlation is not causal and final_spin_other is a residual)

non_attribution: No AP, PX4, OS or host root cause is assigned. The px4 wait at ticks 2000/5504 is off-CPU (wall 6.6-6.9 ms vs CPU 0.79-0.89 ms) and the retained rows do not say what the wait was for.

The tick 107572 stall is measured as a gen-2 GC running inside the px4 wait; the GC record gives thread CPU, not what object graph or allocation triggered it, and the native wait record explicitly excludes acknowledge_ap, barrier/repair_input and record writes.
Native-input rows are retained by slow/periodic rule only; totals over them are not a census of all 27434 groups.

This field is probe-instrumented and diagnostic-only: its 100.050657 ms latch and 269.5 s wall must not be A/B-compared with formal (probe-free) runs, per joint_profile.py:219-220 and the probe overhead caveat.

candidate_pointer.candidate: C1 - one arm/prepare/restore window around the timed segment using only gc.collect() and gc.freeze() at tick-0 preparation, then gc.unfreeze() in the runner's outer finally after all native cleanup. gc.disable() and every threshold change are forbidden, and there is no second collect. Measured basis = the tick 107572 gen-2 GC (24.33 ms thread CPU) whose interval is nested in the px4 native wait, with the 20.75 ms work overrun at the same tick.
candidate_pointer.honest_bound: The 20.8 percent share is one measured event in this single field, and the ~20-26 ms ceiling is an inference from that event, not a measured saving. Reproducibility, necessity and sufficiency are all unproven; the distributed 74.01 ms release excess is untouched, so no pass is claimed.

comparator.contract: consumes the runner's real product result['manager_gc_candidate'] (ManagerGCFreeze.report(), tools/manager_gc_candidate.py sha256 cbf7b0186131c08d4055aea1fcafdb8e7cca36d9acfcb19cdac87938d8786e66) and the side file manager-gc-candidate.json; when both exist they must agree. Validates armed/prepared/restored, froze_own_graph released, original and prepare_check freeze_count 0 with unchanged thresholds, freeze_count before/after 0/1, restore back to 0, activation.clock_tick 0, the armed->prepared->restored event order with no skipped/noop path, and source_sha256 against result['source_sha256']. The comparator never creates or converts gc-freeze.json and never asks the runner to change.
comparator.positive_fixture: the contract positive case calls the real ManagerGCFreeze with an injected FakeGC module; that report is a test fixture, not a new field or retained evidence

unresolved_gap.statement: The field attributes the cumulative creep between two buckets but not to a phase: 25.70 ms of work overrun (3 events, one with a measured GC) plus 74.01 ms of release excess spread over 27433 intervals (mean 2.7 us) whose per-attempt overrun never exceeds 0.323 ms. The probe phases measure the whole wait (including the legitimate sleep and the designed ~1 ms final spin), not the excess portion, so the retained data cannot say which of sleep overshoot, mid-wait health call, or post-spin dispatch produces the residual 2.7 us per group.
unresolved_gap.to_close: a per-attempt excess decomposition (excess versus phase, not only whole-wait phase) plus wake-to-run/scheduler evidence, which this field does not record.

limitations: Only offline reads of the retained diagnostic field; the derived CPU extract is not an original.
Diagnostic probe overhead is included in all timings; absolute lateness is not comparable with formal fields.
The two deliverables of this module are this analysis and docs/plan/33-rate-measured-candidate-20260912.md; nothing here closes or re-opens #83.
